narrative.overview:
The app is a near-black poster sheet ruled by a yellow-tinted modular grid. Each view has one subject (the overview's today pair, the day view's step card), one cadmium-yellow title, and yellow crosshairs that lock onto the subject's corners. Behind everything, ground.js draws the poster itself: grid hairlines with dots on the crossings, crosshairs and arrow marks, charcoal plates with halftones, black discs and a ring, yellow filaments meeting in a junction, and the day's number as a ghost. The ground carries no information.

Components come from the owner's Datum system (vendored in site/dm/bundle.css): cut panels and frames, hairlines, uppercase mono labels, dot-matrix numerals. The Excimer colours are applied on top, dark only. The page is dense but reads in order: big title, hero frame, next-step panel, then sections under arrow-mark headers. It avoids the generic dark dashboard of equal cards and neon accents.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only. Near-black paper, charcoal plates, one cadmium yellow.
Structure drawn in 1px hairlines. No shadows, glows or blur.
Square corners or 45-degree cuts. No rounded boxes.
Bold, tightly tracked Saira for titles. Uppercase IBM Plex Mono for labels, buttons and facts.
A poster ground behind the page. Text never sits on it bare.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: Signal goes on the live thing, the view's one title and the marks that lock onto the subject. Never use it for decoration. Each view has one filled yellow action.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Every colour comes from dm/tokens.css. Never hard-code a colour.

rules.name: The CSS Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are uppercased by text-transform. The DOM text stays in sentence case.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Text never sits bare on the ground. Give it a --paper plate (background plus spread).

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No shadows, glows, gradients or blur. Linear gradients appear only as hard-stop fills (a button's wipe, a chamfer, hatching).

dos: Do give every view exactly one signal title and one filled signal action.
Do put a --paper plate under any text that overlaps the ground.
Do draw structure in 1px --rule hairlines, and use --grid / --grid-mark for the poster's yellow-tinted lines.
Do cut corners at 45 degrees (10 / 16 / 32px) where a shape needs character.
Do set labels, buttons, tags and facts in uppercase IBM Plex Mono through CSS.
Do use only plain glyphs for marks (↗ → ✓ ✕ ■ □ ▶ + / > _ [ ]).
donts: Don't round a box. Every radius is 0 except dots.
Don't use shadows, glows, gradients or blur.
Don't spend signal on decoration or second actions. Use --alert only for what needs attention.
Don't hard-code a colour, and don't add a light theme.
Don't put information on the ground beyond the day's ghost number.
Don't use emoji in the UI.
